title: Moss Galleries in Maine opens an exhibition of work by Robert Neuman
summary: Moss Galleries presents Expressive Roots, an exhibition celebrating the remarkable six-decade career of American artist Robert S. Neuman (1926–2015). Timed to coincide with what would have been the artist’s 100th birthday, the exhibition brings together works that reveal Neuman’s restless experimentation and distinctive approach to abstraction. Expressive Roots is on view at Moss Galleries in Falmouth, Maine, through October 17. Emerging from the rugged landscape of the American West, Neuman developed into a distinctive voice in Abstract Expressionism, creating a body of work that balanced painterly spontaneity with rigorous draftsmanship. Throughout his career, he continually explored new visual languages, moving between loose, gestural brushwork and tightly structured geometry while drawing inspiration from landscape, memory, architecture, symbols, and the natural world. “Robert Neuman was an arti

title: Cavalier Gallery marks 40th anniversary with exhibitions of Harry Benson, Bruno Lucchesi and Paul G. Oxborough
summary: Cavalier Gallery will mark its 40th anniversary this fall with three exhibitions at its West 57th Street location, bringing together photography, sculpture and contemporary realist painting in a program spanning October through December. The anniversary comes four decades after the gallery began as a small operation in Stamford, Connecticut. It has since expanded to locations in New York, Greenwich, Nantucket and Palm Beach. After establishing earlier Manhattan spaces on Madison Avenue and East 72nd Street, Cavalier opened its flagship at 3 West 57th Street in 2013 and has also developed a public art program placing large-scale sculpture in locations around Manhattan. The fall season begins with Harry Benson: Milestones, opening October 5 and continuing through November 6. title: Historic restitution: Japanese citizen voluntarily returns ancient Mesoamerican mask to Mexico
summary: A Mesoamerican stone mask that left Mexico decades ago and eventually surfaced in Japan is set to return home following its voluntary restitution by a Japanese collector. The anthropomorphic mask, believed to date to the Late Preclassic period, roughly 700 to 230 BC, was handed over to the Mexican Embassy in Japan on September 10, 2026. Mexican officials say it is the first archaeological object to be restituted to the country from Japan. According to a preliminary assessment by Mexico’s National Institute of Anthropology and History, or INAH, the mask was likely made in the northern part of what is now the state of Guerrero. Its style and manufacturing technique point to a Mesoamerican origin, although specialists say a more detailed examination will take place once the object arrives in Mexico. title: McNay Art Museum awarded $500,000 grant from Kronkosky Charitable Foundation to advance accessibility
summary: The Kronkosky Charitable Foundation has awarded the McNay Art Museum a $500,000 grant to support enhanced accessibility across the institution’s 25-acre campus and expand access to its digital and programmatic offerings. Structured in two phases, the grant funds an organization-wide accessibility assessment followed by the development and implementation of a prioritized plan for improvements. The McNay will begin work immediately, engaging recognized accessibility consultants with experience serving museums and cultural institutions. Their findings will inform customized recommendations grounded in national best practices and current research. In the second phase, the McNay will evaluate the recommendations and begin implementing those that will make the greatest difference for visitors, ensuring the work moves beyond assessment to meaningful and lasting change. title: New Flammarion book explores India's living traditions of craft, color and design
summary: For textile designer Peter D’Ascoli, India is not simply a source of motifs or materials. It is a place where art, ritual, architecture and daily life remain closely intertwined, and where centuries-old traditions continue to shape contemporary design. That idea is at the heart of India: A Journey Within and Without , a new large-format volume from Flammarion pairing D’Ascoli’s writing with photographs by Ambroise Tézenas. The 352-page book, illustrated with 370 color images, will be published in the United States on October 6, following its September 30 release in France and ahead of its October 8 publication in the United Kingdom. Rather than attempting an encyclopedic survey of Indian art, D’Ascoli presents the country through the eyes of a designer who has spent decades working with its artisans and studying its decorative traditions. title: Three Tang publications win AIGA honors
summary: The Tang Museum at Skidmore College announces that three of its recent publications have been honored in AIGA’s 50 Books | 50 Covers of 2025 competition. The recognition of Paula Wilson: Toward the Sky’s Back Door , Forms of Awakening: Tibetan Art from the Jack Shear Collection , and 3-D Doings: The Imagist Object in Chicago Art 1964–1980 brings the Tang’s total number of AIGA-winning publications to eight. The three were selected by jurors from more than 500 entries in the 2025 competition. Paula Wilson: Toward the Sky’s Back Door, the first major monograph on the multidisciplinary artist, was designed by Morcos Key in close collaboration with Wilson and exhibition curator Rebecca McNamara. title: A simple breakfast, an extraordinary story
summary: At first glance, there is nothing particularly remarkable about this meal. A loaf of crusty bread has been cut open. A diced herring sits on a bright red plate alongside butter, pork, a couple of onions and a glass of beer. It is a simple meal, but there is something familiar about it. It feels as though someone has just stepped away from the table and might return at any moment. Painted in the first half of the seventeenth century by the artist known only as P. v. Plas, Peasant Breakfast belongs to a tradition of still lifes known as ontbijtjes, or breakfast pieces. There is no silver or fine porcelain here. The brown bread tells us this is a modest table, but that does not make it any less beautiful. title: Basquiat's Ancient Scientist leads the Autumn Auction Season in Asia selling for US$9.8M
summary: On 29 September 2026, Christie's opened its Autumn season in Asia with the Hong Kong 20th/21st Century Evening Sale, achieving HK$726,421,000 / US$92,589,911, up 28% year-on-year. The auction was led by Jean-Michel Basquiat's Ancient Scientist, which sold for HK$76,975,000 / US$9,811,264, the most valuable work sold at auction in Asia this Autumn, with bidding from across regions. Featuring a compelling selection of works by leading names in Eastern and Western modern and contemporary art, the Evening Sale was 100% sold by lot. The top ten lots included strong performances for works by Zao Wou-Ki, Yayoi Kusama, Paul Cézanne, Chu Teh-Chun and Liu Ye, reflecting the diversity of the sale and the breadth of collector's interests across categories. title: Sotheby's unveils J.M.W. Turner's defining Italian masterpiece in Rome
summary: Today, within the richly adorned walls of Rome’s baroque Palazzo Rondinini, Sotheby’s unveils J.M.W. Turner’s masterpiece Rome, from Mount Aventine (1836) – a painting that ranks among the very greatest of Turner’s late works, and one of very few paintings of this calibre remaining in private hands. On the last occasion that canvas changed hands it established a new benchmark price for the artist’s work. This December, when the painting comes to auction at Sotheby’s London with an estimate in the region of £50 million, it is set to do the same again. With its three-day exhibition now at the Palazzo Rondinini in Rome (29 September to 1 October), the painting will become the most valuable work of art ever exhibited by any auction house in Italy. title: Van Gogh and Cézanne lead $450 million Blaquier-Arrieta Collection at Sotheby's
summary: A private collection of Impressionist and Modern art that has remained largely out of public view for decades will come to auction at Sotheby’s in New York on November 18, led by major works by Vincent van Gogh and Paul Cézanne. The Blaquier-Arrieta Collection comprises 12 works and is expected to realize around $450 million. Its two highest-valued paintings are Van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs, estimated in the region of $180 million, and Cézanne’s Arlequin, estimated in the region of $120 million. Neither has been publicly exhibited for more than half a century, and Sotheby’s says both could set new auction records for their artists. The collection was assembled by Carlos Pedro Blaquier and Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier, who regularly traveled to London during the 1970s, when major Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings could still be acquired through leading dealers. title: Smashing windows with flowers: Pipilotti Rist's landmark 1990s video art takes center stage in Bilbao
summary: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao presents Pipilotti Rist: Ever is Over All, an exhibition centered on the Swiss artist’s video installation of the same name. This video installation brings to a close the Museum’s Film & Video program. Pipilotti Rist has been a central figure within the international video art scene for several decades. She created her first audiovisual works in the 1980s, drawing inspiration from music films, pop culture, emerging media technologies and video art. Early in her career, she developed a distinctive visual language with a powerful sensory and emotional impact. Presented at the 47th Venice Biennale in 1997, where it earned Rist international recognition and acclaim, Ever is Over All is one of her most iconic video installations and a landmark in the history of late 20th-century video art. title: Museum Ludwig marks 50th anniversary with major survey on Black diaspora and European modernism
summary: To mark its 50th anniversary, the Museum Ludwig is staging a major interdisciplinary survey exhibition that explores the connections between the art of the international Black diaspora and European modernism. The exhibition features modernist and contemporary works by artists of the Black diaspora through a host of international loans that are presented in dialogue with pieces from the Museum Ludwig collection. These works include paintings, sculptures, drawings, literature, and music, highlighting the diversity of artistic expression that served as a platform for cultural exchange and engagement at the beginning of the twentieth century. The title of the exhibition is borrowed from the writings of the African American sociologist W. E. B. Du Bois. title: Four decades of abstraction: Anita Shapolsky Gallery opens major group retrospective
summary: Anita Shapolsky Gallery, founded in 1982, was among the first galleries to reintroduce and champion abstract art at a time when Minimalism and Pop Art dominated the contemporary art scene. Continuing this longstanding commitment to abstraction, the gallery presents its new exhibition, “Abstract Legacy II: Agaist All Odds,” on view from September 30th, 2026 through February 21st, 2027. Anita Shapolsky Gallery, established in the early 1980s in SoHo, began as a new gallery determined to discover and support strong and distinctive artists. At a time when Minimalism and Pop Art dominated the art world, Anita Shapolsky chose to focus on abstract art. Many of the artists the gallery began exhibiting had, over the years, shown at the Martha Jackson Gallery, Betty Parsons Gallery, and many important American and international institutions. title: Upper Belvedere presents Asta Gröting's video installation 'Things' in historic Carlone Hall
summary: Things, a work by German sculptor and media artist Asta Gröting, concludes the series of exhibitions CARLONE CONTEMPORARY at the Upper Belvedere, which General Director Stella Rollig initiated in 2018 and has curated ever since. It is the first show in the series to feature a video installation. Seemingly random things float upward in an unpredictable sequence against a brilliant blue summer sky—gravity has been suspended. The video Things features sixteen organic and inorganic objects that soar in slow motion through the air in a high arc. In the CARLONE CONTEMPORARY exhibition series, they take over the sky in the Baroque ceiling fresco by Carlo Innocenzo Carlone. title: Museum of Decorative Arts and Design in Riga explores geometric structure in new jewelry exhibition
summary: The Museum of Decorative Arts and Design in Riga continues the pop-up exhibition series Spectrum, introducing current developments in Latvian jewelry art. Visitors are invited to see the third exhibition titled Architecture of Lines from 1 October to 13 December 2026. Following the exhibition Beautiful Nature, where jewellery and objects were presented as findings, samples or hybrids between the organic and synthetic world, the next exhibition in the series, Architecture of Lines, focuses on geometric line as one of the fundamental elements in the structure of jewellery – as contour, construction, rhythm, and drawing in space. The exhibition features jewellery artists Māris Auniņš, Jānis Brants, Vladislav Chistyakov, Andris Lauders, Una Mikuda, Anita Savicka, Paula Treimane, and Jānis Vilks. title: Hans van Manen collection reveals the choreographer's eye for photography, Pop Art and geometric abstraction
summary: The private collection of Hans van Manen, the celebrated Dutch choreographer whose spare, psychologically charged ballets influenced generations of dancers, will come to auction at Venduehuis der Notarissen in The Hague on October 14. Extending across more than 80 lots, the group offers an unusually intimate view of Van Manen not only as a choreographer, but as a photographer, collector and participant in the postwar European art world. Presented as the Hans van Manen Estate within Venduehuis’s Post-War & Contemporary Art sale, the collection moves freely between photography, Pop Art, geometric abstraction and works closely connected to Van Manen’s theatrical career. title: Sabrina Amrani consolidates its Madrid programme in Carabanchel with the opening of new spaces
summary: Sabrina Amrani announces a new chapter in the gallery’s development, bringing its entire Madrid operation together in Carabanchel, on the gallery’s fifteenth anniversary. Following the definitive closure of its spaces in central Madrid, Sabrina Amrani, Sabrina Amrani Projects, Sabrina Amrani Editions and the gallery’s new offices are now concentrated on Calle Sallaberry, creating a cluster of complementary spaces dedicated to exhibitions, experimentation, collaboration, editions and the day-to-day work of the gallery. The move completes a process that began in 2019, when Sabrina Amrani opened a 600- square-metre space in Carabanchel conceived for exhibitions of institutional scale. title: Joshua Campbell Torrance named head of Fenimore museums
summary: Fenimore Art Museum and Fenimore Farm and Country Village announce Joshua Campbell Torrance as their new President and CEO effective September 28, 2026. Torrance joined the museums in January 2026 as Senior Vice President to begin the leadership transition process. This position represents a professional homecoming for Torrance. As a student at the Cooperstown Graduate Program, he interned at Fenimore Art Museum. He studied under and was a mentee of Dr. Paul S. D’Ambrosio. D’Ambrosio is retiring as President and CEO after over 40 years with the museums. Torrance was his hand-picked successor. Torrance is coming to Fenimore Art Museum and Fenimore Farm with over 26 years of experience in museum leadership. He served as the Executive Director of Woodlawn Museum, Gardens

title: Sikkema Jenkins & Co. announces representation of Pulitzer Prize winner Raven Chacon
summary: Sikkema Malloy Jenkins announced the representation of Raven Chacon. Raven Chacon is a Pulitzer-Prize winning composer, performer, and installation artist from Fort Defiance, Navajo Nation. Through musical and visual compositions, Chacon explores the complex interactions between people, space, and sound. His works are often site-specific, engaging the material and sonic qualities of a given place to make perceptible what has been historically silenced or left out of the frame: legacies of colonial conquest and extraction, Indigenous memory, cultural narratives, and acts of resistance. Raven Chacon’s first solo exhibition at Sikkema Malloy Jenkins ‘Scores for Coming Storms’ was on view May 14 – June 20, 2026. Raven Chacon was born in 1977 in Fort Defiance, Navajo Nation. title: Art Gallery of Ontario announces 2027 exhibition line up
summary: Today, the Art Gallery of Ontario announced its exhibitions on view in 2027. Bringing together exceptional art and artists from Ontario and around the world, the museum presents nine new, original exhibitions. These exhibitions debut at an exciting moment as the museum looks ahead to the opening of the Dani Reiss Modern and Contemporary Gallery in 2027. Designed to significantly increase space for the AGO’s growing collection of modern and contemporary art, this is the seventh expansion the museum has undertaken since its founding in 1900. “2027 is a big year for the AGO with the opening of the Dani Reiss Modern and Contemporary Gallery. title: Sotheby's Modern & Contemporary South Asian Art Sale in London totals $26.2m
summary: Sotheby’s Modern & Contemporary South Asian Art auction in London totaled £19.8 million / $26.2 million, with a 99% sell-through rate and 89% of works sold above their high estimate. The auction marks the department’s highest total in its more than 30-year history, surpassing the previous record achieved in London in September 2025.* Manjari Sihare-Sutin, Sotheby’s Worldwide Head of Modern and Contemporary South Asian Art, said: “This has been an extraordinary sale for the department — our highest total in history, surpassing the record we set in London only last year. With nine new artist records, the results reflect both the depth of the market and the increasingly international appreciation for South Asian art. title: Elisa Montessori survey in Rome traces more than seven decades of artistic experimentation
summary: A major exhibition devoted to Italian artist Elisa Montessori has opened at the Casino dei Principi at the Musei di Villa Torlonia, bringing together more than 100 works spanning painting, drawing, artist’s books, site-specific interventions and loans from public and private collections. Titled Elisa Montessori. Nel corso del tempo (Elisa Montessori. Over the Course of Time), the exhibition runs through February 28, 2027, and surveys the long career of the Genoa-born artist, who has lived and worked in Rome for much of her life. Rather than presenting a conventional chronological retrospective, the exhibition is conceived as something closer to an autobiographical journey. title: LA Modern Auctions to offer personal collection of renowned conductor and composer
summary: In honor of renowned conductor and composer Michael Tilson Thomas (1944–2026), LAMA presents MTT: A Musician’s Life, The Michael Tilson Thomas Collection on October 15. Closely following the San Francisco Symphony’s “A Concert for MTT” on October 2, this presentation celebrates the extraordinary life of the visionary musician, cultural force, and twelve-time Grammy Award winner. Bringing together objects that surrounded and inspired MTT in his residences and throughout his career, this collection offers a portrait of a creative life that extended far beyond the concert hall. Michael Tilson Thomas was Music Director of the San Francisco Symphony, Principal Conductor of the London Symphony Orchestra, and Co-Founder and Artistic Director of the New World Symphony.
